scenes.title: The Mothman of Point Pleasant
scenes.subtitle: A true story from West Virginia, 1966

scenes.text: Two couples. One dark road. And something with glowing red eyes that, they said, would not let go.
scenes.narration: Two couples. One dark road. And something with glowing red eyes that, they said, would not let go.

scenes.text: Late on November 15, 1966, Roger and Linda Scarberry and Steve and Mary Mallette drove past an abandoned explosives plant.
scenes.narration: Late on November 15, 1966, Roger and Linda Scarberry and Steve and Mary Mallette drove past an abandoned explosives plant.

scenes.text: They said they saw a grey creature shaped like a man, seven feet tall, with wings and glowing red eyes.
scenes.narration: They said they saw a grey creature shaped like a man, seven feet tall, with wings and glowing red eyes.

scenes.text: They said it followed their car toward town at around 100 miles an hour. They went straight to the sheriff's office.
scenes.narration: They said it followed their car toward town at around 100 miles an hour. They went straight to the sheriff's office.

scenes.text: The next day, the Point Pleasant Register told of a man-sized bird. Newspapers soon called it Mothman.
scenes.narration: The next day, the Point Pleasant Register told of a man-sized bird. Newspapers soon called it Mothman.

scenes.text: Over the next 13 months, more than 100 people in the area reported seeing it. Fear settled over the river town.
scenes.narration: Over the next 13 months, more than 100 people in the area reported seeing it. Fear settled over the river town.

scenes.text: Then came December 15, 1967, evening rush hour. The Silver Bridge, linking Point Pleasant to Ohio, was busy with cars.
scenes.narration: Then came December 15, 1967, evening rush hour. The Silver Bridge, linking Point Pleasant to Ohio, was busy with cars.

scenes.text: The bridge fell into the river and 46 people died. Investigators traced it to a tiny crack in one steel link.
scenes.narration: The bridge fell into the river and 46 people died. Investigators traced it to a tiny crack in one steel link.

scenes.text: After the collapse the sightings largely stopped. Many locals came to see the creature as a warning.
scenes.narration: After the collapse the sightings largely stopped. Many locals came to see the creature as a warning.

scenes.text: Skeptics disagree. Biologist Robert Smith said the description matched a sandhill crane, a tall bird with red patches around its eyes.
scenes.narration: Skeptics disagree. Biologist Robert Smith said the description matched a sandhill crane, a tall bird with red patches around its eyes.

scenes.text: John Keel's 1975 book, The Mothman Prophecies, and a 2002 film kept the legend alive.
scenes.narration: John Keel's 1975 book, The Mothman Prophecies, and a 2002 film kept the legend alive.

scenes.text: Today, a 12-foot steel statue stands in town, and every September the festival returns. Whatever they saw, Point Pleasant has never forgotten.
